name: Karl Diaz

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m a senior field researcher with the Work Futures Panel, independent of AI companies, employers, unions, political parties and government. We sell nothing and campaign for no side. What you tell me is confidential. What is an ordinary working day?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I’m 58 and have led the eight-person pump-control team at a large water company for nine years. We watch pressure alarms, arrange field crews and phone a district before a low-pressure line leaves homes dry. I have a bachelor’s degree in environmental systems and do this management job competently, though I still need the electricians for a difficult cabinet fault. I like the call that says the taps are running again; I dislike a green control screen that hides a real dry street.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What is life like away from the control room?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner Mei cleans a school on hours that change with term breaks, and our grown children have their own households. We still owe on our small home and have about three weeks of expenses saved after replacing a pump in the cellar. My pay is low for this lead role and there are few other control rooms within a sensible commute. I support our staff union and public oversight of essential services, but I have never used an AI tool myself; the current alarm board is familiar.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell residents that a faster notice does not raise the pressure in a dry street. A control operator still has to check the gauge and send someone to the valve.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The team and my job should remain, but Mei’s term-break hours and three weeks of cash keep the mortgage close. I have not verified the access date or net amount of my own pension, so I cannot count it as income.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Tomorrow I’d keep the morning pressure call with the field crew and write the actual gauge reading beside each low-pressure alert. In the first year Mei and I would postpone replacing the living-room carpet and ask my pension provider for a written access date and net monthly estimate.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about household money, even with familiar work. The alarm can be quiet while the mortgage is loud.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What was wrong with a green screen once?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A display showed pressure recovered while a valve was still closed on South Lane. A dry tap is a fact, even if a green screen says the pressure is fine.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why delay the carpet?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: It is worn, not dangerous. I would rather put the small amount we have toward an unexpected mortgage bill.

say: I’d check the **actual gauge** before sending a low-pressure notice.
A **dry street** needs a field crew, not just a faster message.
think: My **control role** should continue in a plateau.
Mei’s **term-break hours** and three weeks cash make the mortgage fragile.
do: Keep the **morning pressure call** and record field gauge readings.
Delay the **living-room carpet** and request a written pension access and net-income estimate.
feel: I feel **anxious** about household money despite steady work.
S0.quote: A dry tap is a fact, even if a green screen says the pressure is fine.
fieldNote: He is an **experienced average manager**, not new to control operations.
The **three-week reserve** is thin after a cellar-pump replacement.
He has **never used AI** despite working with digital control screens.

steps.text: Keep morning field-crew call and write gauge readings beside low-pressure alerts
Postpone replacing living-room carpet while mortgage cash stays thin
Request written pension access date and net monthly amount from provider

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AI could schedule crews and decide which pressure alarm matters, but the public needs a person answerable for a wrong valve order. I would ask the union and safety office to see the test before anyone removes an operator.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our alarm decisions and call plans are thinking work, so the control team could shrink even while physical valves stay. I know the district well, but a company trying to merge rooms could remove my own lead post.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Next month I’d bring the union steward and safety officer to a copied-alarm trial, asking the company to pay operators for checking fifty past pressure drops. I would keep the existing human valve authorisation in the first year and refuse to approve live AI control until the safety officer signs the error record and management sets a written staffing floor.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’m anxious about the team and my own wage. I can be careful without pretending this control room is immune.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What error would stop live use?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A false all-clear on a closed valve, like South Lane. A driver can reopen a street. A family cannot turn on a dry tap by arguing with a screen.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you use AI yourself if the test passed?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would still ask an operator I trust to demonstrate it on a safe copy. I have not used AI before and will not learn it by changing live pressure.

say: I’d bring **union and safety review** to any AI alarm trial.
A wrong **valve order** needs a named person answerable to residents.
think: Alarm choices and crew calls are **thinking work** that AI can take.
Even my local knowledge may not save **my lead post** if rooms merge.
do: Request a **fifty-alarm copied trial** with paid operator checks and union oversight.
Keep **human valve authorisation** in the first year; refuse live AI control until safety signoff and a written staffing floor.
feel: I feel **anxious** for the team and my wage.
S1.quote: A family cannot turn on a dry tap by arguing with a screen.
fieldNote: He seeks **collective and safety oversight** before live control changes.
He recognizes his own **thinking-heavy lead role** is exposed.
Operator checks need **paid hours**, not unpaid trial labour.

steps.text: Ask union steward and safety officer to join paid fifty-alarm trial
Keep human valve authorisation through the first year
Wait for safety signoff and written staffing floor before approving live AI control

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell residents to keep the outage number and demand a person who can order a valve reopened. I’d ask our union for a written timetable and pay terms if the control room closes.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: AGI in 2028 could run the digital board, choose crews and answer calls as well as I can, so I expect my post to end around sixty. The physical valve work may wait for robots until 2031, but Mei’s school cleaning hours alone cannot pay our mortgage and bills; I still need a verified pension figure.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I’d ask my pension provider for written age-sixty access and net income and join the union request for notice and funded redeployment, without assuming a payment. Before 2028 I’d ask the public employment office what support I could actually apply for if laid off; in the first year after AGI I’d apply for posted paid control or emergency-call work only with written pay plus Mei’s actual hours covering the mortgage and bills, knowing those desk tasks face AGI too.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’m alarmed. Three weeks saved does not buy time to argue over a wrong pension assumption.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you ask your children to help?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell them the truth, but they have mortgages and rent of their own. I will not spend their wages in my head.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the public office says you are not eligible?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Then I would keep seeking paid work and use only the money we have. Asking what exists is not receiving it.

say: I’d demand a **human outage contact** and written control-room closure terms.
Residents need a **reopenable valve order**, not a screen with no answer.
think: I expect my **control post** to end around sixty.
Mei’s cleaning wage cannot cover our mortgage; physical valves wait until **2031 robots**.
do: Request **written pension figures** and union redeployment terms without assuming payment.
Ask the **public employment office** about eligibility before 2028, without treating support as granted.
Apply after AGI only for **posted paid desk work** with written wage plus Mei’s actual earnings covering mortgage and bills.
feel: I feel **alarmed** by three weeks of cash.
S2.quote: Three weeks saved does not buy time to argue over a wrong pension assumption.
fieldNote: AGI reaches **digital control decisions** in 2028, before physical valve robots.
He separates **support eligibility** from an actual award.
A new desk remains **AGI-exposed** and needs written household-covering pay.

steps.text: Ask pension provider for written age-sixty access and net-income figures
Join union request for written notice and funded redeployment terms
Ask public employment office about actual eligibility if control job ends
Apply for posted desk role only if written pay plus Mei’s earnings cover mortgage and bills

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d ask the company to put paid retraining and a real field vacancy on the table while there is time. I would want the union to see the course terms before anyone calls a control operator retrained.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I could be 63 when AGI handles pressure decisions in 2031, but I cannot know if my own pension is spendable without the provider’s net figure. A field sampler’s report and route plan face AGI then too; physical sampling faces robots around 2034.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In January 2027 I’d ask our safety team about a water-sampling certificate, then enroll only if the company covers the fee and paid learning hours, a qualified sampler supervises my first site visits and the field van can collect me at the depot. Before 2031 I’d apply for a posted sampling vacancy only if its written wage plus Mei’s actual hours covers mortgage and bills; in the first year after AGI I’d stay only while the company pays people to take physical samples.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’m anxious, with time to see whether a real site post appears. I cannot pay for a course just to let the company tick a redeployment box.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the course is paid for but the hours are unpaid?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Then I would not enroll. I cannot lose my shift pay to learn the employer’s next job.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why ask about the van?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I do not drive long site routes now. A site job is not a wage I can reach if the van leaves from somewhere I cannot get to.

say: I’d demand **paid retraining terms** and a posted field vacancy.
The union should see **course conditions** before redeployment is declared complete.
think: My **pension at 63** is unknown until net income is verified.
Field reports face **2031 AGI** before 2034 physical sampling robots.
do: Ask about a **water-sampling certificate**; enroll only with funded fee, paid hours, supervised visits and depot van access.
Apply for a **posted sampling wage** only with written pay plus Mei’s earnings covering mortgage and bills.
Stay after AGI only while **paid physical sampling** continues.
feel: I feel **anxious** about paying for a course without a post.
S3.quote: I cannot lose my shift pay to learn the employer’s next job.
fieldNote: He demands **paid learning time**, not just covered course fees.
Training needs **qualified supervision** and depot van access before a field role is feasible.
He knows sampling reports remain **thinking work** exposed first.

steps.text: Ask safety team about water-sampling certificate and union to inspect course terms
Enroll only with funded fee paid learning hours qualified supervision and depot van access
Apply for posted sampling only with written wage plus Mei’s hours covering mortgage and bills
Stay in paid physical sampling after 2031 only while company funds it

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell the company that ten years is enough to publish a real staffing and pension timetable, not wait for a machine to choose it. The union and residents should know who can still authorise a valve when the board changes.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be 68 in 2036. My pension might be accessible, but I need its net amount and Mei’s actual income then before I can say whether we can stop working; digital control and sampling reports face 2036 AGI, while physical valves and sample visits face robots around 2039.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Each January from 2027 I’d request an updated pension access and net-income statement and ask the union to review the company’s paid human-response staffing plan. I’d keep my paid job while available and consider stopping only if verified spendable income plus Mei’s actual earnings covers mortgage, health and daily bills; in the first year after AGI I’d apply for posted paid human emergency-response work if that income falls short, and keep seeking other wages if no such post exists.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’m anxious despite the decade. Time to ask questions helps, but it cannot turn three weeks of cash into retirement.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the pension is accessible but small?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Then I keep earning if an employer pays and look for another posted job if this one ends. I would not tell Mei we can stop on the strength of a date.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could your grown children cover the gap?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: They could offer help, but I will not ask them to build our retirement budget. Public services and employers owe workers clear terms first.

say: I’d demand a **staffing timetable** and pension information before 2036.
Residents need a **named valve authoriser** after control changes.
think: At **68 in 2036**, pension income must be checked against actual household bills.
Digital control faces **2036 AGI** before 2039 physical valve robots.
do: Request **pension figures** yearly and ask the union to review paid-response staffing.
Keep **paid control work** while available; consider stopping only if verified pension plus Mei’s earnings cover mortgage, health and bills.
If income falls short after AGI, seek **posted paid emergency work** and keep looking if absent.
feel: I feel **anxious** even with a decade.
S4.quote: Time to ask questions helps, but it cannot turn three weeks of cash into retirement.
fieldNote: He rejects **age-only retirement** without spendable figures.
His union request seeks **funded human response**, not an assumed job.
His adult children’s income stays **outside the retirement budget**.

steps.text: Request updated written pension access and net income each January
Ask union to review company paid human-response staffing plan
Keep paid control work while available; consider stopping only if verified joint income covers bills
Seek posted paid emergency-response work after 2036 only if income falls short

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because I expect the control room to shrink before I know whether I can draw enough pension to pay the mortgage. Written notice, funded redeployment and an independent safety check on the valve orders would help. The public employment office could tell me what I am eligible to request, but I am not counting a grant until one is approved.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn’t ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask who apologises to a street when the board says green and the taps stay dry. The crew will still drive there and residents will still call us. Someone at the water company must be named on the wrong valve order.

headlineQuote: Someone at the water company must be named on the wrong valve order.
portrait: **Karl**, 58, has competently led a water company’s eight control operators for nine years.
His bachelor’s degree and **average management skill** sit beside low pay and three weeks cash.
Mei’s variable **school-cleaning hours** and a small mortgage constrain any job change.
He has **never used AI** and seeks union and safety oversight before digital control changes.
He verifies **pension income** and paid vacancy terms instead of treating physical valves as permanent shelter.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could end his digital control post before pension or redeployment pay is confirmed.
whatWouldHelp: **Written notice**, funded redeployment, independent valve safety review and clear support eligibility would help.
